scenes.heading: Data Security
scenes.narration: Data security protects information from unauthorized access and misuse across its entire lifecycle, using layered controls for identity, encryption, and access.

scenes.heading: Layers of defense
bullets: Encryption in transit with TLS everywhere
Encryption at rest with managed keys
Least-privilege access with roles and policies
Auditing and monitoring of every access
scenes.narration: Encryption in transit protects data as it moves between services using TLS. Encryption at rest protects stored data using keys managed in a secure key service, ideally with rotation. Least-privilege access ensures each principal has only the permissions it truly needs, expressed through roles and fine-grained policies. And continuous auditing records who accessed what, so anomalies can be detected and investigated.

scenes.heading: Coarse vs fine-grained access
scenes.narration: Coarse-grained access controls grant permissions at the table or database level, which is simple to administer but often over-exposes sensitive columns to people who only need a few fields. Fine-grained controls enforce row-level and column-level policies, and can mask or tokenize personal data so analysts see only what they are authorized to see. Fine-grained control requires more policy management, so reserve it for sensitive datasets while using coarse grants for low-risk data.

scenes.heading: Defense in depth for a request
scenes.narration: When a request arrives, the platform first authenticates the identity, confirming who is asking. It then authorizes the request against access policies to decide what that identity may see. Data is decrypted using keys from the key management service. Row filters and column masks are applied so the caller receives only permitted data. Finally the access is logged so security teams have a complete, tamper-resistant audit trail.

scenes.heading: Protecting PII specifically
bullets: Mask, tokenize, or hash sensitive fields
Restrict raw PII to a few roles
scenes.narration: Personal data needs targeted handling beyond general controls. First you must discover and classify which columns contain personal information, since you cannot protect what you have not identified. Sensitive fields are then masked, tokenized, or hashed so most consumers never see raw values. Access to unmasked personal data is restricted to a small set of trusted roles with a clear business need. And analytics workloads are steered toward pseudonymized or aggregated data, so most work never touches raw identifiers at all.

scenes.text: Assume breach and layer your defenses; encryption, least privilege, and auditing together limit the blast radius of any single failure.
scenes.narration: Design as if a breach will happen and layer your defenses, because encryption, least-privilege access, and thorough auditing working together are what limit the blast radius when any single control fails.
